$comment: Stack-side evidence for the WoT specification requirements whose proof is an
OPC UA implementation. The specification ledgers mark these entries
'pendingStackTests', because a specification cannot name a test in a
repository it does not build. This file names them.
One entry per specification requirement, carrying that requirement's
statementHash: the hash is over the normalized sentence, so a restatement
upstream invalidates the mapping here rather than silently keeping evidence
for something the specification no longer says.
Those hashes are checked rather than merely carried: wot-spec-statements.json
vendors the same digests, copied from the specification's own requirement
ledgers at the pinned commit rather than re-derived from its prose, and
'statementInventory' below pins that file by SHA-256. Editing a statementHash
in one file and not the other therefore fails, as does adding or dropping an
identifier on one side. Regenerate or check the inventory with
tools/wot-spec/Get-WotStatementDigests.ps1 against a spec-drafts checkout
holding the pinned commit; -Verify reproduces it and fails on any byte that
moved.
A 'gap' entry is a requirement this stack does not yet prove. It is stated,
not omitted: the whole point of replacing a blanket "pending" is that what
remains unproved is enumerated and countable.
Every named test is resolved by reflection in the assembly it names, and has
to be something NUnit will actually run. Re-pin the source commit when the
specification lands a new revision.
The referenced fixtures are behavioral evidence, not a Full profile claim.
Explicit gaps distinguish deferred validation, excluded policy evidence,
optional capability evidence and deployment/HA obligations from executed tests.

requirements.gap: The stock registry advertises and exercises EventDriven automatic refresh. Periodic and implementation-defined Scheduled modes are not claimed by this evidence.
Group/Version authorization and disclosure-policy internals are excluded from this review; public snapshot tests do not certify the full policy.
Optional Core SemanticChange behavior is not certified by the current WoT evidence.
Full conformance is not claimed: deferred full-schema/compatibility checks and optional semantic-change evidence remain explicit.
Full TD/TM JSON Schema validation is explicitly deferred; syntax, admission and projection checks are not full format-validation evidence.
Explicit projection compatibility/admission is tested, but the combined requirement also requires full legacy TD validation, which is deferred.
Complete local restart recovery is tested. Publication-state replication between independent HA replicas is not exercised or claimed by these local runtime witnesses.
Management-access policy implementation is excluded from review; lowered-security test hosts are not conformance evidence for production access policy.
Secure/read-only deployment channel policy requires host-specific evidence beyond the loopback test configuration.
Group read-authorization policy internals are excluded; per-deployment disclosure configuration is not certified.
Operator deployment policy is not established by implementation unit tests.
Legacy management access-policy internals are excluded from review; no security conformance claim is inferred from test-host access overrides.
Endpoint trust/bounds controls are exercised, but the combined requirement includes deferred full-format validation of generated legacy TD input.
The optional WOTC-SemanticChange conformance unit is not certified by the retained WoT evidence; no Full profile claim is made.
The optional WOTC-SemanticChange conformance unit and its complete negative event matrix are not certified by the retained WoT evidence.
Publication planning, capture, units and recovery are exercised, but the complete algorithm includes deferred full-format and compatibility-policy validation.
